newsitem.title: japan: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN WINS RECORD SIXTH WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN WINS RECORD SIXTH WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Germany's Gunda Niemann broke her own world record in winning an unprecedented sixth title at the world speedskating championships on Sunday, the first world mark set on slap skates.
Ids Postma of the Netherlands finished fourth in the 10,000 metres to clinch the men's title ahead of Japan's Keiji Shirahata.

Niemann, who first strapped on the revolutionary skates less than a month ago, shaved 1.574 points off her three-year-old record with wins in the 1,500, 3,000 and 5,000 metres and a runner-up placing in the 500 metres.
A double gold medallist at the Albertville Olympics, Niemann finished with 165.708 ponnts after beating Tonny de Jong of the Netherlands by more than four seconds in the 5,000 metres on Sunday.
"I don't know if the record was due to the skates or not," said the 30-year-old veteran. "I used them because they're new and if you don't try them you don't know what you might be missing."
Postma, who finished with 157.906 points, led the men's event throughout the three-day competition at the new M-Wave arena built to host speed skating events at next year's Nagano Olympics.
After placing second in the 500 metres on Friday, Postma added a win in the 1,500 and an eighth-place finish in the 5,000 on Saturday.
"Ive been really really close before, so it's really good to win here," said Postma, runner-up for the world title last year and in 1994.
Shirahata, who was .560 points behind Postma, won bronze medals in the 500 and 5,000, was sixth in the 1,500 and fifth in the 10,000. Frank Dittrich of Germany placed third overall.
Dutch-born Bart Veldkamp, who competes for Belgium, won Sunday's 10,000 metres ahead of Dittrich and Lasse Saetre of Norway. All set personal records on the new skates.
Postma said he would reconsider his decision not to switch.
"I've seen three skaters today skate very fast on the new skates," said Postma. "Im quite sure they're better for long distances."
Niemann's compatriot Claudia Pechstein, another recent convert, took third place in the women's 5,000 metres to place second overall with 168.179 points.
De Jong, who unseated Niemann as the dominant female distance speed skater earlier this season pioneering the new skates, was third with 168.206 points.
After losing to De Jong at the European championships last month, Niemann skipped a World Cup competition in Baselga di Pine, Italy, to try the new skates herself.
Niemann said her poor starts on the slap skates were offset by a more relaxed feeling in her legs during the longer races.
Eight of 12 women in the 5,000 metres, including the top four finishers, wore the new skates, whose blade releases at the heel to allow skaters a fuller push against the ice.
The skates are certain to be allowed at the Nagano Olympics, said International Skating Union (ISU) president Ottavio Cinquanta, who said skaters should be allowed to creatively improve performance.
"If the skates help improve performance, why not allow them?" said Cinquanta. "It doesn't seem that they help artificially."

Current ISU regulations specify only that blades cannot be heated with any mechanical device. "If we forbid these skates, we should also specify the maximum length of the blade, or forbid moving the blade, or make regulations about the boots," said Cinquanta.
"We are in favour of transparency in the sport," he said.
